findings.message: Replacing the `_lambda_argument_depths` stack with a simple counter `_lambda_arguments` removes the depth check (`self._lambda_argument_depths[-1] == self.depth`). When a lambda defines a default parameter value containing a colon (such as a dictionary literal like `lambda x={1: 2}: x` or a slice like `lambda x=a[1:2]: x`), the colon inside the default value will match line 983 because `_lambda_arguments > 0`. This prematurely decrements `self.depth` and `_lambda_arguments` at the wrong nesting level, causing corrupted depth tracking and incorrect code formatting.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the `_lambda_argument_depths: List[int]` stack and check `self._lambda_argument_depths and self._lambda_argument_depths[-1] == self.depth` before popping and decrementing depth.

findings.message: Replacing the `_for_loop_depths` stack with a simple counter `_for_loop_variable` removes the check verifying that the `in` keyword occurs at the same nesting depth as the corresponding `for` keyword (`self._for_loop_depths[-1] == self.depth`). If an `in` keyword appears inside a nested expression within the loop target (e.g. `for (x if a in b else y) in z:`), `maybe_decrement_after_for_loop_variable` will trigger prematurely at a higher depth level, incorrectly decrementing `self.depth` and corrupting bracket depth tracking.

findings.suggested_fix: Restore the `_for_loop_depths: List[int]` stack and check `self._for_loop_depths and self._for_loop_depths[-1] == self.depth` before popping and decrementing depth.

findings.message: Changing `if token in ('def', 'for'):` to `if token == 'def':` breaks `async for` tokenization. When `token` is `'for'` and `stashed` is `'async'`, the `async` word will no longer be yielded as an `ASYNC` token (it falls through as a `NAME` token), causing syntax parsing failures for `async for` statements.
findings.suggested_fix:
if token in ('def', 'for'):
                         if (stashed
                                 and stashed[0] == NAME
                                 and stashed[1] == 'async'):

                             if token == 'def':
                                 async_def = True
                                 async_def_indent = indents[-1]

findings.message: A '# fmt: on' comment on a child node inside `container` will be ignored. For AST `Node` objects, `container.prefix` only returns the prefix of its first leaf. If `# fmt: on` occurs on a subsequent child/leaf within `container`, `is_fmt_on` will evaluate to `False`, causing the loop to yield the entire `container` block as unformatted and skip processing `# fmt: on`.
findings.suggested_fix: Reintroduce inspection of `container.children` to detect `# fmt: on` comments inside child nodes before yielding the parent `container`.

findings.message: `container = container.next_sibling` was moved inside the `else` branch. When `contains_fmt_on_at_column(container, leaf.column)` is True and no child causes an early `return`, the `for child in container.children` loop finishes, but `container` is never updated to `container.next_sibling`. The outer `while` loop then runs again with the exact same `container`, creating an infinite loop.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure `container = container.next_sibling` is executed after the `if/else` block on every iteration of the `while` loop.
